display.title: Shabbos Shira and Tu B'Shvat: A Person Is Like a Tree
display.summary_short: This Shabbos we hear the Song at the Sea, and it is also Tu B'Shvat: like a tree, a person must bring fruit, our Torah and good deeds.
display.summary_long: A short holiday talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi explains that this Shabbos is Shabbos Shira, when the Torah reading includes Az Yashir, the song the Jewish people sang after leaving Egypt, and everyone, young and old, should be in shul to hear it. This Shabbos is also Tu B'Shvat, the New Year for Trees. We eat fruits, especially those of Eretz Yisroel, say the brachah Borei Pri Ha'eitz and, on a new fruit, Shehecheyanu. Why celebrate the trees' new year? Because the Sages teach that a person is like a tree of the field: the most important part of a tree is its fruit, and our fruits are good deeds, learning more Torah and doing more mitzvos.
display.lesson: Like a fruit tree, a person should bring fruit: more Torah and more mitzvos.

date.note: Clip of episode 360 (dated 01-17-89); Shabbos Shira fell on Tu B'Shvat, 21 January 1989.

sources_cited.note: 'A person is like a tree of the field', as explained by the Sages.

quality.notes: Speaks of 'this Shabbos' as both Shabbos Shira and Tu B'Shvat, true only in some years.
